summary: Friedrich Haag worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler at the University of Zurich, and also attended Göttingen and Berlin. He was a Dozent at Zurich (1873–1884) and professor of classical philology at Bern (~1884–1914).
Friedrich Hirth worked in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the universities of Berlin, Leipzig, and Greifswald, and held a post at Columbia University from around 1902 to 1917.

Active in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies, Müller studied under Brockhaus, Burnouf, Bopp, Schelling, and Wilson at Leipzig, Berlin, and Paris. He spent his career at Oxford, becoming Professor of Comparative Philology in 1854 and 1883–1900.

Friedrich Müller was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Vienna under Anton Boller and at Göttingen. After positions at the Hof- und Staatsdruckerei and imperial and university libraries, he became a professor at the University of Vienna in 1869.

Friedrich Rückert worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and under Franz Bopp, later serving as professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1826) and professor of Arabic at Berlin (1841–1849).

Friedrich Schlegel worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Göttingen and Leipzig, and under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He held posts at the University of Jena (~1800–1801), Cologne (~1804–1807), and TU Dresden.
Friedrich Weller specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under August Conrady from circa 1910 to 1915 and became Ordinarius for Indology at Leipzig University in 1928.

Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph von Schelling was a philosopher who studied at the Tübinger Stift, University of Tübingen, and Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena, Würzburg, Erlangen-Nuremberg, Munich, and Berlin.

Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl worked in linguistics. He studied at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg, and held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1829–1833), Breslau (~1833–1839), Bonn (~1839–1865), and Leipzig (~1865–1875).

Friedrich Windischmann was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar. He studied at Munich and under Christian Lassen at Bonn, and served at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1836–1861) and as Vicar General for the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising (~1848–1861).
Friedrich Zarncke worked in linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University (~1843–1847) and later held posts at the University of Rostock and Leipzig University (~1852–1891).

Friedrich von Spiegel was an Iranian and Indology scholar. He studied under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, Hermann Brockhaus, and Christian Lassen at Bonn, and held a post at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from circa 1849 to 1890.

Frits Staal worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Amsterdam and Banaras Hindu University, and held posts at the University of Amsterdam, MIT, and as professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~1968–1991).
Fritz Johaentgen was a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher who studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (1919–1923). He held posts at Munich (~1934–1936) and at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1947–1969).

Fujio Taniguchi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Nagoya University under Musashi Tachikawa, also studying under several other teachers, and was a lecturer at Chiba College of Health Science in 1991.

Fumihiko Sueki specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo, later serving there as professor (attested 1988–2003) and professor emeritus, with subsequent posts at Nichibunken and Sōkendai (~2009–2015).
Fumimaro Watanabe was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He held academic posts at Ryukoku University, Hanazono University, Nagoya University, and Aichi Gakuin University.

Fumimasa Fukui was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Waseda University and under Paul Demiéville at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He was a professor at Waseda University from circa 1978 to 2005.
Fumio Enomoto is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a research assistant at Kyoto University (~1981–1987) and as a professor at Osaka University (~1998–2017).
